comment:
* Holds a PKCS#8 key, for example a private key
 *
 * @author Dave Brownell
 * @author Benjamin Renaud

variables.name: serialVersionUID
variables.comment: use serialVersionUID from JDK 1.1. for interoperability

variables.name: key
variables.comment: The key bytes, without the algorithm information

methods.name: public static PKCS8Key parse(DerValue in) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Binary backwards compatibility. New uses should call parseKey().

methods.name: public static PrivateKey parseKey(DerValue in) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Construct PKCS#8 subject public key from a DER value. If * the runtime environment is configured with a specific class for * this kind of key, a subclass is returned. Otherwise, a generic * PKCS8Key object is returned. * *

This mechanism gurantees that keys (and algorithms) may be * freely manipulated and transferred, without risk of losing * information. Also, when a key (or algorithm) needs some special * handling, that specific need can be accomodated. * * @param in the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo value * @exception IOException on data format errors

methods.name: protected void parseKeyBits() throws IOException, InvalidKeyException
methods.comment:
* Parse the key bits. This may be redefined by subclasses to take * advantage of structure within the key. For example, RSA public * keys encapsulate two unsigned integers (modulus and exponent) as * DER values within the key bits; Diffie-Hellman and * DSS/DSA keys encapsulate a single unsigned integer. * *

This function is called when creating PKCS#8 SubjectPublicKeyInfo * values using the PKCS8Key member functions, such as parse * and decode. * * @exception IOException if a parsing error occurs. * @exception InvalidKeyException if the key encoding is invalid.

methods.name: static PrivateKey buildPKCS8Key(AlgorithmId algid, byte[] key) throws IOException, InvalidKeyException
methods.comment:
* Factory interface, building the kind of key associated with this
     * specific algorithm ID or else returning this generic base class.
     * See the description above.

methods.name: public String getAlgorithm()
methods.comment: * Returns the algorithm to be used with this key.

methods.name: public AlgorithmId getAlgorithmId()
methods.comment: * Returns the algorithm ID to be used with this key.

methods.name: public final void encode(DerOutputStream out) throws IOException
methods.comment: * PKCS#8 sequence on the DER output stream.

methods.name: public synchronized byte[] getEncoded()
methods.comment: * Returns the DER-encoded form of the key as a byte array.

methods.name: public String getFormat()
methods.comment: * Returns the format for this key: "PKCS#8"

methods.name: public byte[] encode() throws InvalidKeyException
methods.comment:
* Returns the DER-encoded form of the key as a byte array.
     *
     * @exception InvalidKeyException if an encoding error occurs.

methods.name: public void decode(InputStream in) throws InvalidKeyException
methods.comment:
* Initialize an PKCS8Key object from an input stream. The data * on that input stream must be encoded using DER, obeying the * PKCS#8 format: a sequence consisting of a version, an algorithm * ID and a bit string which holds the key. (That bit string is * often used to encapsulate another DER encoded sequence.) * *

Subclasses should not normally redefine this method; they should * instead provide a parseKeyBits method to parse any * fields inside the key member. * * @param in an input stream with a DER-encoded PKCS#8 * SubjectPublicKeyInfo value * * @exception InvalidKeyException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public void decode(byte[] encodedKey) throws InvalidKeyException
private void readObject(ObjectInputStream stream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Serialization read ... PKCS#8 keys serialize as
     * themselves, and they're parsed when they get read back.

methods.name: static void encode(DerOutputStream out, AlgorithmId algid, byte[] key) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Produce PKCS#8 encoding from algorithm id and key material.

methods.name: public boolean equals(Object object)
methods.comment: * Compares two private keys. This returns false if the object with which * to compare is not of type Key. * Otherwise, the encoding of this key object is compared with the * encoding of the given key object. * * @param object the object with which to compare * @return true if this key has the same encoding as the * object argument; false otherwise.

methods.name: public int hashCode()
methods.comment:
* Calculates a hash code value for this object. Objects
     * which are equal will also have the same hashcode.
